production.note: One US model year. BMW: "The 2011 BMW 1 Series M Coupe will be available in limited quantities" at US dealers "in Spring, 2011". Cars.com lists only the 2011 model year for the 1 Series M (carscom-1-series-m-years).

displacementL.note: 2,979 cc. BMW UK technical data: "Effective displacement cm3 2,979". The US release says "3.0-liter".

fuel.note: Gasoline direct injection ("High Precision direct injection"); inferred from the release.

transmission.note: "A close ratio 6-speed manual transmission is used for power transmission to the rear wheels"; the only transmission.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Maximum output of 335 hp (250 kW) is delivered at 5,900 rpm." The overboost function raises torque only ("This temporary torque peak of 369 lb-ft"), not the power rating.

weightLb.note: Preliminary (manufacturer preliminary figure). Quote (BMW of North America release, 9 December 2010): "The new 1 Series M Coupe weighs in at 1,495kg DIN (3,296 lbs, preliminary)". Cars.com (database) gives the same: "Base Curb Weight: 3,296 lbs" (carscom-2011-1-series-m). BMW UK technical data: "Curb weight -DIN / EU- kg 1,495 / 1,570" (bmw-uk-1m-techspecs). No final BMW figure was found; the car was sold for one model year. Motor Authority (Nelson Ireson) reports a car weighed at 3,351 lb with a full tank (a measured figure, not used; motorauthority-1m-weighed).

discrepancies.reason: DIN vs EU weight. Encycarpedia's 3,461 lb is exactly BMW's EU figure (1,570 kg, which includes a 75 kg driver; bmw-uk-1m-techspecs: "1,495 / 1,570"). 3,296 lb is BMW's DIN figure (1,495 kg), which BMW of North America published.
discrepancies.resolution: 3,296 lb used: the guide uses DIN, not EU, weights.

reviewNotes: Weight 3,296 lb is BMW's DIN figure marked 'preliminary'; the car was sold for one model year, so no final figure exists. Kept with weightQualifier 'preliminary', following the owner's Corvette ZR1 (C7) decision.
